svg.text: Sheet 2 of 2 · which net rides which pin, and where each module unplugs
LD1 DOUT crosses the wrist to LD2 DIN as LED_DATA_HAND
J2-6 lands on the strip ground here:
the second conductor serves the elbow run only
the motor pair crosses the sleeve untouched
the whole glove comes off on one plug
its own strap, so it never bridges the wrist
THE RULES THAT MAKE THIS SAFE TO PULL APART IN A DARK ROOM
Four plugs per arm plus the one at the switch: J2 and J3 at the elbow, J4 and J5 at the wrist, J6 in the palm.
No two connectors on one arm share both family and pin count: PH-2 (2.0 mm), ZH-2 (1.5 mm), SM-2 (2.5 mm), SM-5, SM-6.
The two SM-2 plugs are identical on purpose - same net, so cross-mating them only shortens the motor run.
SW1 off, or the cell out, before you mate or unmate anything. Feeding data into an unpowered strip is what kills pixel 0.
